lines.before: **Hard rules:** batch at G3 (triage and diagnose everything, then fix roots). **One sweep:** one large sweep per branch; a fix that changes behaviour ships with a test that fails before it (rule:test-value); CI runs the full suite and auto-fix handles red. A second pass is the owner's call; escapes are measured next build. Findings are fixed in the build that finds them. A low or medium that cannot be finished carries only on the owner's yes, first next build. A high or critical never carries: it is fixed before the PR (found after it: on the open PR), or the owner accepts it.
lines.after: **Hard rules:** batch at G3 (triage and diagnose everything, then fix roots). **One sweep** per branch; a high, critical, security or owner-rule fix ships with a failing-first test, a low or medium only if a real input shows it (else `no test: no real input`; rule:test-value); CI runs the full suite and auto-fix handles red. A second pass is the owner's call; escapes are measured next build. Findings are fixed in the build that finds them. A low or medium that cannot be finished carries only on the owner's yes, first next build. A high or critical never carries: it is fixed before the PR (found after it: on its PR), or the owner accepts it.

lines.before: - **Fix sets:** the fix check confirms each fix's test fails on the code before it. Why: with no re-sweep, the failing-first test is what catches a half-done fix.
lines.after: - **Fix sets:** each test a fix names must fail on the code before it; CI's test check states it per fix. Why: with no re-sweep, the failing-first test is what catches a half-done fix.
